newsitem.title: ZAIRE: French minister says Zaire refugee crisis unsolved.
newsitem.headline: French minister says Zaire refugee crisis unsolved.

text.p: French humanitarian affairs minister Xavier Emmanuelli said on Tuesday Zaire's refugee crisis had not been resolved despite the exodus of Rwandan Hutus.

"There has been a massive return of refugees to Rwanda but this is far from resolving all the existing problems. There are still many refugees and displaced people in need of help," Emmanuelli told reporters in the Zaire capital Kinshasa.
Emmanuelli on Tuesday met Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo before flying to the eastern city of Kisangani.
Zairean soldiers defeated in a month of fighting between the army and Banyamulenge Tutsis in eastern Zaire have been making their way to Kisangani, as have many displaced Zaireans.
France has paid for food to be delivered from Kisangani to deserting soldiers on the road to encourage them to allow aid through, U.N. sources told Reuters.

Two relief convoys carrying food and medicines destined to assist displaced Zaireans and Hutu refugees and resupply medical centres on the road east, were due to leave Kisangani on Tuesday, according to the U.N. sources.

Emmanuelli said France still favoured the presence of a multinational force in Zaire to help bring aid to hundreds of thousands of displaced Zaireans, as well as Hutu refugees who have not returned to Rwanda.

"The principle of sending a multinational force has been voted in (by the U.N. Security Council). Certainly the situation is evolving, and I understand the member states are making operational adjustments to the plans. We ourselves are presently involved in these adjustments and negotiations," he said.
Rwanda has cited the refugee exodus to back its opposition to an international force and the United States also signalled a change of mind about sending troops to the region.
Emmanuelli did not say whether France would act independently of the United Nations if plans to send the force are abandoned.
Zaire's government spokesman, Boguo Makeli, accused Rwanda on Tuesday of trying to scupper U.N. plans for the force.

He said the Kigali government feared that the presence of the force would reveal evidence that Rwanda had violated Zaire's territorial integrity. Zaire accuses Rwanda's Tutsi-led army of helping the Banyamulenge Tuitsi rebels to seize a border strip.
Boguo denied charges based on documents found in the deserted Mugunga refugee camp that Zaire was assisting soldiers from the former Rwandan regime in their plans to re-invade Rwanda.
